title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Unrepresented Persons
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is acting for a plaintiff in Small Claims Court. The defendant is self-represented. During a settlement discussion, the unrepresented defendant asks the paralegal for their opinion on whether a proposed settlement is fair. How must the paralegal respond?
options: Give an honest, objective opinion to facilitate the settlement.
Advise the unrepresented person that the paralegal represents only the plaintiff, whose interests are opposed to the defendant's, and urge the defendant to seek independent legal representation.
Tell the defendant that the settlement is generous and they will lose at trial.
Refuse to speak to the unrepresented person completely.
questions.explain: Under Rule 4.05 (Unrepresented Persons), when a paralegal deals on behalf of a client with an unrepresented person, the paralegal must make it clear that they are not protecting the unrepresented person's interests and must advise them to obtain independent legal representation.
